summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/66)

data.translation: He says, ‘Shut up!’, he says, ‘I will get you a better one’.
data.ref: MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/66

rationale: New formal Imperativ cell; preserves the command with its reassurance instead of an isolated token.

evidence.cite: MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/66

data.turoyo: Ono gṭəryono, d u malko sokət.
data.translation: Ich werde den König schon zum Schweigen bringen.

rationale: New formal Infectum cell; dependent d-clause has king as subject, while the edition translates the complete causative matrix construction.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (51/62)

data.turoyo: Hano ftəḥle u sefoqo, ḥzele u lišono. Sakət. Omər: "E!"
data.translation: Der König deckte die Schüssel auf, sah die Zunge, und schwieg. "Ja!" sagte er.

rationale: New Preterit Intransitive cell and completed silence in a narrative; the full short context identifies the king and contrasts his next utterance.

data.turoyo: W beʕammi ne, me d aḏiʕi, yawmo tre gsəkti.
data.translation: Wenn die Familie meines Onkels davon hört, nun, nach ein, zwei Tagen werden sie nichts mehr sagen.

rationale: Plural future Infectum adds agreement evidence beyond the singular dependent clause and shows cessation of objections.

summary: The inherited skt article is a draft with no formal stems or numbered senses. I.1 structures its already noted silence meaning; inherited notes, etymology and personal-communication uncertainty remain unchanged.

sakət/sokət in the same Ritter episode and plural gsəkti across a separate text support a finite verbal borrowing rather than analysis of all occurrences as an invariant interjection. Imperativ Skat alone would not establish that integration.
In 51/58 gṭəryono is the matrix predicate; sokət has u malko as its intransitive subject. The edition rendering zum Schweigen bringen does not make sokət transitive or Stem III.
51/62 pairs completed Sakət with later speech; silence is bounded by context, not a separate lexical sense. 52/56 future gsəkti carries plural agreement with beʕammi.
Confirm integration and exact paradigm of the Arabic-related forms, including whether Skat is a productive Turoyo Imperativ or a retained Arabic command.
The draft personal communication skīt is explicitly uncertain and supplies no present corpus occurrence: confirm its form and box before constructing a Detransitive paradigm.
The inherited gloss also mentions calm down and stay back. Do they have independent Turoyo evidence beyond becoming silent?
The inherited FA_58 and abbreviated 51/58 quotation should be reconciled with the full MAC and Ritter references before editorial deduplication; no unsupported citation replacement proposed.
